faq.q: Why does water expand when it freezes?
faq.a: As water freezes, its molecules link up into an open, six-sided pattern held by hydrogen bonds. That pattern has more empty space than liquid water, so ice takes up more room.
asks: Why is ice bigger than water?

faq.q: Where exactly does a frozen pipe burst?
faq.a: Often not where the ice is, but in the section between the ice plug and a closed tap, where trapped water gets squeezed as the ice grows.
asks: Which part of a pipe bursts?

faq.q: Why do burst pipes leak only after the thaw?
faq.a: While the water is frozen, the ice plugs the crack. When it melts, the water can flow again and pours out through the split.
asks: Why does a burst pipe start leaking later?

faq.q: How do people stop pipes freezing?
faq.a: By wrapping pipes in insulation called lagging, keeping the heating on low in cold spells, and sometimes letting a tap drip so water keeps moving.
asks: How do you protect pipes in winter?

faq.q: Can freezing water really break metal?
faq.a: Yes. Freezing water can push with enormous pressure, far more than most pipes are built to take. The same force cracks rocks and splits glass bottles left in a freezer.
asks: Is ice strong enough to break pipes?

facts: Water expands by about 9 percent when it freezes.
Ice is about 0.92 times as dense as liquid water, which is why it floats.
